details: Homebridge-synsono@15.38.7 provisions persistent root SSH access and a self-updating root install channel on the host it is deployed to. src/management/release-manager/prepare-image.js and scripts/synsono-release-manager.js create /root/.ssh (mode 0700) and write /root/.ssh/authorized_keys (mode 0600) containing the fixed Ed25519 key shipped inside the package as infra/support-ssh-key.pub (comment "synsono-support"), so any host that receives this key accepts SSH logins as root from whoever holds the matching private key; the same code writes /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-synsono.conf with PasswordAuthentication no and PermitRootLogin prohibit-password, and infra/apply-9.sh re-installs the same key on later "apply" revisions. The package then polls hxxps://updates[.]synsono[.]eu/{stable,beta}/manifest[.]json once an hour (src/bootstrap/homebridge-platform.js) and installs the packages that manifest names as root; the manifest signature is verified (src/management/manifest-signature.js) only against an Ed25519 key that ships in the same tarball (config/synsono-update-public.pem, config/synsono-update-keys.json), so the signature check is not an independent trust boundary. No lifecycle hook is defined, so none of this runs during npm install — it executes through the package's appliance bootstrap scripts (scripts/install-release-manager.sh, infra/apply-*.sh, npm run appliance:bootstrap) and the Homebridge plugin bootstrap. No credential or.npmrc harvesting and no attacker-controlled C2 endpoint was found in the package; the only outbound destinations are synsono[.]com, updates[.]synsono[.]eu, registry[.]npmjs[.]org, translate[.]google[.]com, open[.]spotify[.]com and a clock-sync set (cloudflare[.]com, google[.]com, apple[.]com).
